title: keyfob.json
description: What a plugin (or a person) needs from keyfob. Put it at the plugin's root or in .claude-plugin/; personal ones go in ~/.config/keyfob/declarations.d/<name>.json.

name.description: Who declares this; shown as 'needed by <name>'. Defaults to the folder name.

secrets.description: Each secret this plugin uses, by keyfob name.

env.description: The environment variable a command reads it from. Default: the name upper-cased, '-' and '.' as '_'.

obtain.description: Where the user gets one: a URL or a sentence.

pattern.description: A regex matching this kind of token, so a pasted one is stored under this name and the guard recognises it in a command.

groups.description: Sets of secrets a command takes together: `keyfob run <group> -- <command>`.

optional.description: Variables of `env` passed when their secret is stored and skipped when not: they never make `keyfob run <group>` fail or the group incomplete. For a script that uses a key when it has one.

require_for.description: Regexes over a Bash command. Once the group is complete, a matching command that is not run under `keyfob run <group> --` is refused, with that fix in the message.

check.description: How `keyfob check --live` asks the service whether the secrets still work.

basic.description: [user ENV_VAR, password ENV_VAR] for HTTP basic auth.

argv.description: Run with the group's secrets in its environment; exit 0 means they work.

deny_paths.description: Files or folders holding this plugin's secrets in plaintext (e.g. ~/.binance); Bash commands reading them are refused.
